C1.sentence: E_1 = 13.812 and A_1 = 2.798 reproduce, but the pairs still descend -0.40 to -0.11 per 100 it against the single's -0.015, so the unconverged part does NOT cancel in E_int (net up to 0.37 per 100 it, growing with d), and d 12 / 18 ran 800 it while d 15 / 24 and the singles ran 1500.

C2.sentence: the four E(d) and both fits reproduce (sigma 0.973, rms 0.65 vs 0.99; E_pin excluded from E_stat_8, confirmed) and a 1/d term is not detectable (3-parameter fit B = -50 +- 191 with 1 dof), but the ladder mixes 800 and 1500 it runs with d-dependent end slopes: the same-budget (800 it) ladder gives sigma 1.19 and the geometric extrapolation sigma 0.80, so the tension is budget-dependent at the 20 to 30 percent level and the RISING sign is the robust content.

C3.sentence: own interpolated-ring windings at x = 0, +-d/4 and rho 2.2, 4.5 are all 1 (30 rings) and the far sphere r 30 has degree 1.00 to 1.00 (total charge ONE, fixed by the seed and the pinned box shell); the midplane axis gap dips to 0.32 to 0.39 (d 18 above the claimed 0.31 to 0.34) at the innermost lattice cells rho 1.06, so the melted core of radius ~1 is BELOW the lattice resolution h 1.5 (gap 0 or escape on the axis undecidable); the per-core hedgehog degree on a sphere pierced by the +1 line depends on the lift and on how the piercing cap is filled (outward lift: 0.04 to 0.98 on the seed itself; continuity lift: 0.92 to 0.97 on the pinned cores at r 2 to 6), so '+1 per core' is a reading of about 0.95, not an integer invariant, and two such cores sum to the unit far field.

C4.sentence: A_pair reproduces (2.73 to 2.43; the producer's window holds the cores at d 18, 24 and the d 24 tail slope is -5.2, not -4) and the pair's far-field energy beyond r 16 is ONE single's (1.03 to 1.62 times 1.39, not two): the one-far-field reading holds, but that shared far field is worth only 3.8 (r > 8) to 2.1 (r > 12) against the intercept c = -19.4, so the negative E_int is not the far field beyond r 8; the three-zone split (cores = within 4 of a core, string zone, far = r > d/2 + 8) gives E_int = cores [-3.0 to -2.6, flat in d] + string zone [-3.3 at d 12 to 7.4 at d 24, slope 0.90 per unit length] + far [-1.6 to -0.8]: the whole d-dependence is the string zone, the cores do not attract (their term is constant), and the offset is the one-texture-instead-of-two saving spread over all three zones; the right reference for a unit-charge composite is E(d) - E_1 = 6.2 to 17.5 (positive, rising), and the linear law reaches E_1 at d 5.7.

C5.sentence: free E_int -5.79 with the same string reads, but the cores are NOT still at +-7.5: the melted-core centroids sit at +-6.38 in the free field (distance 12.77) against +-7.00 pinned (distance 14.01) and +-7.50 in the seed; the free cores moved 0.62 each toward the midpoint in 1500 it (the field differs from the pinned one by at most 0.049) and the run still descends -0.14 per 100 it: a slow contraction, not a static pair.

C6.sentence: the n48 data support the string (winding 1 on all 30 rings, every d, pinned and free), the absence of a detectable 1/d term and the sign argument against the 8 pi test; but PAIR_LAW_RETIRED is the wrong name for what was measured: the seed normalize(rhat_1 + rhat_2) with the box shell pinned to it has total charge ONE (degree 1.00 on r 30 at every d), so the object is a unit hedgehog whose core is split into two melted half-cores joined by a winding-1 line, not two like charges (whose far field would carry 4 A_1); E(d) - E_1 = 6.2 to 17.5 is the composite's cost over one hedgehog, sigma 0.8 to 1.2 per unit length is budget-dependent (mixed 800 / 1500 it, d-dependent end slopes), and the linear law crosses E_1 at d 5.7, i.e. it predicts a split-core hedgehog CHEAPER than the R16-1 radial one below that d (a core instability of the single, or a bend of the law: d 6 and 9 runs decide); the n64 L96 box (same h 1.5) must show sigma unchanged, E_1 up by only ~0.2 (the r^-4 tail converges: 4 pi A / R) and the intercept unchanged within ~0.5, else the string is the pinned shell's artefact; it cannot resolve the melted core (same h).
